docs.title: MSF Vue
docs.text: This repository contains the MSF Vue package and its companion frontend tooling. It is meant to provide a reusable UI layer built with Vue, shared styling, and component patterns for downstream projects within the broader MSF ecosystem.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
The library is intended to provide:

  • Vue-based reusable component primitives
  • support for styling and integration with a modern frontend stack
  • a shared component story for downstream app work
  • a consistent library package for MSF frontend use cases

docs.title: Repository shape
docs.text:
vue/
├── src/
├── public/
├── tests/
├── cypress/
├── playground/
├── scripts/
├── package.json
├── vite.config.ts
├── mkdocs.yml
├── .github/
└── openwiki/

docs.title: Typical commands
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm lint
pnpm test

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep components reusable and composable
  • separate library code from demo or playground usage
  • document styling and dependency assumptions clearly
  • validate build and test workflows before shipping API changes

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The @msflib/vue package is a Vue-based UI library for the MSF ecosystem. It is organized to support component reuse, frontend integration, and a standard library release flow with Vite and related tooling.

docs.title: Main responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is designed to cover:

  • reusable Vue components and UI primitives
  • library build output in dist/
  • testing and linting support for frontend code
  • shared styling and integration patterns for apps

docs.title: Key stack details
docs.text:
The package uses a modern Vue setup with Vite, ESLint, and Vitest:

"scripts": {
  "build": "vite build",
  "lint": "eslint src playground/src tests",
  "test": "vitest"
}

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm lint
pnpm test

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• keep components focused and composable
  • minimize app-specific logic in the shared library
  • document style and dependency assumptions for downstream users
  • validate both build and test flows before changing public APIs
